title.zh: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝
title.raw: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝 Volume 7 Annals 7: Emperor Fei I

sentences.zh: 前廢帝諱子業，小字法師，孝武帝長子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Fei I, taboo name Ziye, childhood name Fashi, was Emperor Xiao Wu's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei I was named Ziye; his childhood name was Fashi. He was Emperor Xiao Wu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年正月甲申生。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, first month, jiashen day, he was born.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on jiashen day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮尋陽，子業留京邑。

translations.literal: Shizu was stationed at Xunyang; Ziye remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizu held Xunyang, Ziye stayed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十年，世祖入伐元凶，被囚侍中下省，將見害者數矣，卒得無恙。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Shizu entered to attack Yuanxiong; he was imprisoned in the Attendant Censorate lower offices, several times about to be harmed, but in the end was unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when Shizu marched in to punish Yuanxiong, Ziye was held prisoner in the lower offices of the Attendant Censorate. He was several times on the verge of death, yet in the end came through unscathed.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, he was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, Ziye was named Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 始未之東宮，中庶子、二率並入直永福省。

translations.literal: At first he had not yet gone to the Eastern Palace; the Junior Tutor and the two commandants all entered duty at Yongfu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before he moved to the Eastern Palace, his Junior Tutor and the two palace commandants all took duty in Yongfu Province.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，出居東宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, he moved out to dwell in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he took up residence in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: [1]四年，講孝經於崇正殿。

translations.literal: [1] In the fourth year, he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: [1] In the fourth year he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 七年，加元服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he received the cap of adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he underwent the coming-of-age ceremony.

sentences.zh: 八年閏五月庚申，世祖崩，其日，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, intercalary fifth month, gengshen day, Shizu died; that day the Crown Prince assumed the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year, on gengshen day, Shizu died; that same day the Crown Prince ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭解尚書令，加中書監，驃騎大將軍柳元景加尚書令。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing; Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong relinquished the post of Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was appointed Director.

sentences.zh: 甲子，置錄尚書，太宰江夏王義恭錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the office of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was established; Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the office of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was created, with Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong as recorder.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍柳元景加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was given the additional title of Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an office of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was granted an office equal in ceremonial honor to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Director of Danyang Prince of Yongjia Ziren was made Inspector of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Danyang Prince of Yongjia Ziren was appointed Inspector of Southern Yu.

translations.literal: [2] In Ziren's biography 'Southern Yu' is written as 'Southern Yan'.
translations.idiomatic: [2] In Prince of Yongjia Ziren's biography the post is recorded as Inspector of Southern Yan rather than Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 六月辛未，詔曰：「朕以眇身，夙紹洪業，敬御天威，欽對靈命。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xinwei, an edict said: "With this slight person I early inherited the great enterprise, reverently bearing heaven's majesty, respectfully facing the numinous mandate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinwei, an edict said: "I, slight in person, early inherited the great enterprise, reverently bearing heaven's majesty and facing the numinous mandate.

sentences.zh: 仰遵凝緒，日鑒前圖，實可以拱默守成，詒風長世。

translations.literal: Looking up to follow the solidified thread, daily mirroring the former chart, truly one may fold the hands in silence and guard the accomplishment, leaving a lasting wind for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to the settled line of succession and taking the former models as my daily mirror, I might indeed fold my hands in silence, guard what has been achieved, and let good custom endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 而寶位告始，萬宇改屬，惟德弗明，昧于大道。

translations.literal: Yet as the precious throne is just announced, the myriad realms change their allegiance; virtue alone is not bright, and I am obscure to the great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as the throne has only just been taken up and the realm has changed hands, my virtue is not yet clear and I remain blind to the great Way.

sentences.zh: 思宣睿範，引茲簡恤，可具詢執事，詳訪民隱。

translations.literal: Thinking to proclaim the wise model and extend this simple compassion, let the responsible officials be fully consulted and the people's hardships examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to proclaim a wise standard and extend this measure of relief, let all responsible officials be consulted and the people's hardships investigated in detail.

sentences.zh: 凡曲令密文，繁而傷治，[3]關市僦稅，事施一時，而姦吏舞文，妄興威福，加以氣緯舛互，[4]偏頗滋甚。

translations.literal: All crooked ordinances and secret statutes, elaborate and harmful to governance, [3] market tolls and lease taxes applied for a time only, yet corrupt clerks manipulate the text and presumptuously raise authority and blessing; moreover the qi-lines are at odds, [4] and partiality grows ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Crooked ordinances and secret statutes that are elaborate and harm good governance, [3] market tolls and lease taxes meant as temporary measures—yet corrupt clerks twist the wording and presumptuously wield power; and with the qi-lines in disorder, [4] bias grows ever worse.

sentences.zh: 宜其寬傜輕憲，以救民切。

translations.literal: It is fitting to broaden corvée and lighten punishments, to relieve the people's urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée should be eased and punishments lightened to relieve the people's urgent distress.

sentences.zh: 御府諸署，事不須廣，雕文篆刻，無施於今。

translations.literal: The various offices of the imperial storehouse need not be extensive; carved writing and seal-cutting have no place today.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices of the imperial household need not be numerous; carved ornament and seal-cutting have no place in the present age.

sentences.zh: 悉宜并省，以酬氓願。

translations.literal: All should be combined and reduced, to answer the common people's wish.
translations.idiomatic: They should all be consolidated and cut back to answer the people's wish.

sentences.zh: 藩王貿貨，壹皆禁斷。

translations.literal: Princes' trade in goods is entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Trade in goods by imperial princes is forbidden altogether.

sentences.zh: 外便具條以聞。

translations.literal: Outside, let detailed items be prepared and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Let detailed reports be prepared and submitted from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 」戊寅，以豫州之淮南郡復為南梁郡，復分宣城還置淮南郡。

translations.literal: " On the day wuyin, Huainan commandery of Yu province was restored as Southern Liang commandery; Xuancheng was again divided off to re-establish Huainan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " On wuyin Huainan commandery in Yu province was restored as Southern Liang commandery, and Xuancheng was split off again to re-establish Huainan commandery.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以南海太守袁曇遠為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Administrator of Nanhai Yuan Tanyuan was made Inspector of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Administrator of Nanhai Yuan Tanyuan was appointed Inspector of Guang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史晉安王子勛改為江州刺史，中護軍宗慤為安西將軍、雍州刺史，鎮北將軍、徐州刺史湘東王彧為護軍將軍，中軍將軍義陽王昶為征北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on the day jihai, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong Prince of Jin'an Zixun was changed to Inspector of Jiang; Colonel of the Palace Guard Zong Que was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made General of the Guard; General of the Center Prince of Yiyang Chang was made General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jihai, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong Prince of Jin'an Zixun was reassigned as Inspector of Jiang; Colonel of the Palace Guard Zong Que became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu Prince of Xiangdong Yu became General of the Guard; and General of the Center Prince of Yiyang Chang became General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，婆皇國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, the state of Pohuang sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the state of Pohuang sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 崇皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The Honored Empress Dowager was styled Grand Empress Dowager; the Empress was styled Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Honored Empress Dowager was elevated to Grand Empress Dowager, and the Empress to Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，罷南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, the northern and southern imperial speedways were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the northern and southern imperial speedways were abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來所改制度，還依元嘉。

translations.literal: Institutions changed since Xiaojian are to return to the Yuanjia standard.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions altered since the Xiaojian era were restored to the Yuanjia standard.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，追崇獻妃為獻皇后。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞解領司徒。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan relinquished his concurrent post as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八月丁卯，領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day dingmao, General of the Guard Wang Xuanmo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingmao, General of the Guard Wang Xuanmo was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: [5]己巳，以青、冀二州刺史蕭惠開為益州刺史。

translations.literal: [5] On the day jisi, Inspector of Qing and Ji Xiao Huikai was made Inspector of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: [5] On jisi Inspector of Qing and Ji Xiao Huikai was appointed Inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 己丑，[6]皇太后崩。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, [6] the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou [6] the Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 京師雨水。

translations.literal: In the capital region there was flooding rain.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains flooded the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，[7]遣御史與官長隨宜賑卹。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, [7] censors were sent with local officials to give relief as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin [7] censors were dispatched with local officials to provide relief as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，護軍將軍湘東王彧為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinchou, General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinchou, General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was appointed General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以尚書左僕射劉遵考為特進、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Zunkao was made Special Grand Master and Right Honored Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Zunkao was made Special Grand Master and Right Honored Grandee.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，文穆皇后祔葬景寧陵。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Empress Wenmu was enshrined beside the deceased emperor at Jingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Empress Wenmu was enshrined for joint burial at Jingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲戌，太常建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on the day jiaxu, Minister of Ceremonies Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jiaxu, Minister of Ceremonies Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was appointed General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Si.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was appointed Inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: [8]庚辰，原除揚、南徐州大明七年逋租。

translations.literal: [8] On the day gengchen, overdue rents from Yang and Southern Xu for the seventh year of Daming were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: [8] On gengchen overdue rents from Yang and Southern Xu for the seventh year of Daming were remitted.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day yiyou, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: [9]壬辰，以王畿諸郡為揚州，以揚州為東揚州。

translations.literal: [9] On the day renchen, the commanderies within the imperial domain were made Yang province; Yang province was made Eastern Yang.
translations.idiomatic: [9] On renchen the commanderies of the imperial domain were made into Yang province, and Yang province was renamed Eastern Yang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以車騎將軍、揚州刺史豫章王子尚為司徒、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yang Prince of Yuzhang Zishang was made Minister of Works and Inspector of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yang Prince of Yuzhang Zishang was appointed Minister of Works and Inspector of Yang.

sentences.zh: 去歲及是歲，東諸郡大旱，甚者米一升數百，京邑亦至百餘，餓死者十有六七。

translations.literal: In the previous year and this year, the eastern commanderies suffered great drought; in the worst cases a sheng of grain cost several hundred, and in the capital as well over a hundred; of those who starved, six or seven in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous year and this year the eastern commanderies suffered severe drought; in the worst places a sheng of grain cost several hundred cash, and even in the capital over a hundred. Six or seven out of ten of those who starved died.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來，又立錢署鑄錢，百姓因此盜鑄，錢轉偽小，商貨不行。

translations.literal: Since Xiaojian, mint offices were also established to cast coin; because of this the common people illicitly cast as well, and the money became ever more false and small, so that commerce would not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiaojian mint offices had also been set up to cast coin, prompting widespread illicit casting by the people; the money grew ever more debased and small, and trade ceased to circulate.

sentences.zh: 永光元年春正月乙未朔，改元。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongguang, spring, first month, on the day yiwei at the new moon, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, on yiwei at the new moon, the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，省諸州臺傳。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the provincial relay stations were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the provincial relay stations were abolished.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以領軍將軍湘東王彧為衞將軍、南豫州刺史，護軍將軍建安王休仁為領軍將軍，祕書監山陽王休祐為豫州刺史，左衞將軍桂陽王休範為中護軍，南豫州刺史尋陽王子房為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yu; General of the Guard Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General of the Guard; Director of the Palace Library Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made Inspector of Yu; General of the Left Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was made Colonel of the Palace Guard; Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xunyang Zifang was made Inspector of Eastern Yang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu became General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yu; General of the Guard Prince of Jian'an Xiuren became General of the Guard; Director of the Palace Library Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou became Inspector of Yu; General of the Left Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiufan became Colonel of the Palace Guard; and Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xunyang Zifang became Inspector of Eastern Yang.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑，減州郡縣田祿之半。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yichou, the field stipends of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yichou, the field stipends of provinces, commanderies, and counties were cut in half.

sentences.zh: [10]庚寅，鑄二銖錢。

translations.literal: [10] On the day gengyin, two-zhu coin was cast.
translations.idiomatic: [10] On gengyin two-zhu coin was cast.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，罷臨江郡。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiachen, Linjiang commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiachen, Linjiang commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 五月己亥，割郢州隨郡屬雍州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day jihai, Suizhou of Ying province was cut off and attached to Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jihai, Suizhou of Ying province was detached and placed under Yong province.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以後軍司馬張牧為交州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Rear Army Staff Officer Zhang Mu was made Inspector of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Rear Army Staff Officer Zhang Mu was appointed Inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，左軍長史劉道隆為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jisi, Left Army Chief Clerk Liu Daolong was made Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jisi, Left Army Chief Clerk Liu Daolong was appointed Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，安西將軍、雍州刺史宗慤卒。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Zong Que died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Zong Que died.

sentences.zh: 壬午，衞將軍、南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was changed to Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was reassigned as Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: [11]尚書令、驃騎大將軍柳元景加南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: [11] Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was given the additional post of Inspector of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was also made Inspector of Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛酉，越騎校尉戴法興有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: In autumn, eighth month, on the day xinyou, Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry Dai Faxing committed an offense and was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinyou, Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry Dai Faxing was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以尚書僕射顏師伯為尚書左僕射，[12]吏部尚書王景文為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; [12] Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jingwen was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo became Left Vice Director; [12] Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jingwen became Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝自率宿衞兵，誅太宰江夏王義恭、尚書令驃騎大將軍柳元景、尚書左僕射顏師伯、[13]廷尉劉德願。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the emperor himself led the palace guards and executed Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry Liu Yuanjing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo, [13] and Minister of Justice Liu Deyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor personally led the palace guards and put to death Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry Liu Yuanjing, Left Vice Director Yan Shibo, [13] and Minister of Justice Liu Deyuan.

sentences.zh: 改元為景和元年。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to the first year of Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 文武賜位二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks in precedence.

sentences.zh: 以領軍將軍建安王休仁為安西將軍、雍州刺史，衞將軍湘東王彧還為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was returned to Inspector of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was reassigned as Inspector of Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，司徒、揚州刺史豫章王子尚領尚書令，射聲校尉沈文秀為青州刺史，左軍司馬崔道固為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Minister of Works and Inspector of Yang Prince of Yuzhang Zishang took charge of the Masters of Writing; Colonel of the Archers Shen Wenxiu was made Inspector of Qing; Left Army Staff Officer Cui Daogu was made Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Minister of Works and Inspector of Yang Prince of Yuzhang Zishang assumed direction of the Masters of Writing; Colonel of the Archers Shen Wenxiu was appointed Inspector of Qing; and Left Army Staff Officer Cui Daogu was appointed Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「昔凝神佇逸，磻溪讚道，湛慮思才，傅巖毗化。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, an edict said: "In former times, concentrating the spirit and waiting in stillness, Panxi praised the Way; deep thought sought talent, and Fuyan assisted in transformation.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai an edict said: "Of old, when one concentrated the spirit and waited in stillness, Panxi praised the Way; when one pondered deeply to seek talent, Fuyan aided in transformation.

sentences.zh: 朕位御三極，風澄萬宇，資鈇電斷，正卯斯戮。

translations.literal: I occupy the three extremities, the wind is clear through the myriad realms; relying on the axe and lightning stroke, at the hour of mao the guilty are slain.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the three extremities and the wind is clear through the myriad realms; with axe and lightning I strike, and at the mao hour the guilty are executed.

sentences.zh: 思所以仰宣遺烈，俯弘景祚，每結夢庖鼎，瞻言板築，有劬日昃，無忘昧旦。

translations.literal: Thinking how to look up and proclaim the legacy left behind, look down and extend the glorious reign, each night I dream of the cauldron in the kitchen and gaze toward the planks on the bank; I toil from sun to sun and do not forget the hour before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to look up and proclaim the legacy I have received and look down to extend the glorious reign—night after night I dream of the cauldron in the kitchen and gaze toward the planks on the riverbank; I toil from dawn to dusk and do not forget the hour before dawn.

sentences.zh: 可甄訪郡國，招聘閭部：其有孝性忠節，幽居遯棲，信誠義行，廉正表俗，文敏博識，幹事治民，務加旌舉，隨才引擢。

translations.literal: Let commanderies and states be examined and village districts recruited: those with filial conduct and loyal integrity, dwelling in seclusion and living in reclusion, with trustworthiness, sincerity, righteous conduct, and incorruptible uprightness that mark the customs, with literary quickness and broad knowledge, and with ability in affairs and governance of the people—let them all be especially commended and promoted according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: Let every commandery and district be searched and local communities canvassed: anyone showing filial piety and loyal integrity, living in seclusion, or demonstrating trustworthiness, righteous conduct, and incorruptible example; anyone quick in letters and broad in learning, capable in affairs and fit to govern the people—let such persons be specially commended and promoted according to their talents.

sentences.zh: 庶官克順，彝倫咸叙。

translations.literal: Then the officials will be able to comply, and the norms will all be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Thus officials may perform their duties properly and the norms be kept in order.

sentences.zh: 主者精加詳括，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Those in charge should examine carefully in detail and report what accords with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let those in charge examine the matter carefully in detail and report what accords with my intent.

sentences.zh: 」以始興公沈慶之為太尉，鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史王玄謨為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was made Grand Marshal; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji Wang Xuanmo was made General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was appointed Grand Marshal; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji Wang Xuanmo was appointed General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以石頭城為長樂宮，東府城為未央宮。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Stone City was made Changle Palace; the Eastern Headquarters was made Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Stone City was made Changle Palace and the Eastern Headquarters Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 罷東揚州并揚州。

translations.literal: Eastern Yang was abolished and merged into Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yang was abolished and merged back into Yang province.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以北邸為建章宮，南第為長楊宮。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, the Northern Residence was made Jianzhang Palace; the Southern Mansion was made Changyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the Northern Residence was made Jianzhang Palace and the Southern Mansion Changyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 以冠軍將軍邵陵王子元為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: General Who Champions the Army Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan was made Inspector of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Champions the Army Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan was appointed Inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，原除吳、吳興、義興、晉陵、琅邪五郡大明八年以前逋租。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, overdue rents from Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langye before the eighth year of Daming were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu overdue rents from Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langye before the eighth year of Daming were remitted.

sentences.zh: 己丑，復立南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, the northern and southern imperial speedways were restored.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the northern and southern imperial speedways were restored.

sentences.zh: 九月癸巳，車駕幸湖熟，奏鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day guisi, the imperial carriage visited Hushu and martial music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guisi, the emperor visited Hushu and martial music was performed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以南兗州刺史永嘉王子仁為南徐州刺史，丹陽尹始安王子真為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Inspector of Southern Yan Prince of Yongjia Ziren was made Inspector of Southern Xu; Director of Danyang Prince of Shian Zizhen was made Inspector of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Inspector of Southern Yan Prince of Yongjia Ziren was appointed Inspector of Southern Xu, and Director of Danyang Prince of Shian Zizhen Inspector of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞免為庶人，賜死。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was demoted to commoner and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was reduced to commoner status and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以兗州刺史薛安都為平北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Inspector of Yan Xue Andu was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Inspector of Yan Xue Andu was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 丁未，衞將軍湘東王彧加開府儀同三司，特進、右光祿大夫劉遵考為安西將軍、南豫州刺史，寧朔將軍殷孝祖為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was given the additional title of Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an office of his own; Special Grand Master and Right Honored Grandee Liu Zunkao was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yu; General Who Pacifies the North Yin Xiaozu was made Inspector of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu was granted an office equal in ceremonial honor to the Three Dukes; Special Grand Master and Right Honored Grandee Liu Zunkao became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yu; and General Who Pacifies the North Yin Xiaozu Inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以前梁、南秦二州刺史柳元怙復為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, the former Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin Liu Yuanyou was again made Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen former Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin Liu Yuanyou was reappointed Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 己酉，車駕討征北將軍、徐州刺史義陽王昶，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, the imperial carriage campaigned against General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xu Prince of Yiyang Chang; within and without, the realm was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the emperor marched in person against General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xu Prince of Yiyang Chang, and the realm was placed on full alert within and without.

sentences.zh: 昶奔于索虜。

translations.literal: Chang fled to the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chang fled to the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，右將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐進號鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, General of the Right and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was advanced in rank to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai General of the Right and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以安西長史袁顗為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Chief Clerk of the Pacifying West Army Yuan Yan was made Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Chief Clerk of the Pacifying West Army Yuan Yan was appointed Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以左民尚書劉思考為益州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Director of the Left Bureau of the People Liu Sikao was made Inspector of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Director of the Left Bureau of the People Liu Sikao was appointed Inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 是日解嚴，車駕幸瓜步。

translations.literal: That day the alert was lifted; the imperial carriage visited Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the alert was lifted and the emperor visited Guabu.

sentences.zh: 開百姓鑄錢。

translations.literal: The common people were permitted to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Private casting of coin was permitted among the people.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸亥，曲赦徐州。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on the day guihai, Xu province was given a partial amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on guihai, Xu province received a partial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was appointed General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 己卯，東陽太守王藻下獄死。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, Administrator of Dongyang Wang Zao was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Administrator of Dongyang Wang Zao was thrown into prison and died there.

sentences.zh: 以宮人謝貴嬪為夫人，加虎賁靸戟，鸞輅龍旂，出警入蹕，實新蔡公主也。

translations.literal: The palace woman Worthy Consort Xie was made Lady, with Tiger Guards bearing halberds, imperial carriage and dragon banners, going out and in with imperial escort; she was in fact Princess of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: The palace woman Worthy Consort Xie was made a Lady, granted Tiger Guards with halberds, an imperial carriage and dragon banners, and escort when going out and in—she was in fact Princess of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以鎮西大將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made General Who Pacifies the Army and given an office equal in ceremonial honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army with an office equal in ceremonial honor to the Three Dukes.

translations.literal: [14] In all editions "General Who Pacifies the West" reads "General Who Pacifies the North"; corrected per Xiuyou's biography and the ninth-month xinhai entry.
translations.idiomatic: [14] All editions had "General Who Pacifies the North" where the text should read General Who Pacifies the West; the correction follows Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou's biography and the ninth-month xinhai entry.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬辰，寧朔將軍何邁下獄死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day renchen, General Who Pacifies the North He Mai was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renchen, General Who Pacifies the North He Mai was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 新除太尉沈慶之薨。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Grand Marshal Shen Qingzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, who had just been appointed Grand Marshal, died.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，立皇后路氏，四廂奏樂。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Lady Lu was established as empress, with music in all four side-halls.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Lady Lu was installed as empress, with music performed in all four side-halls.

sentences.zh: 赦揚、南徐二州。

translations.literal: Yang and Southern Xu provinces were granted amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was granted to Yang and Southern Xu provinces.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍建安王休仁加特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was given the additional titles of Special Grand Master and Left Honored Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made Special Grand Master and Left Honored Grandee.

sentences.zh: 中護軍桂陽王休範遷職。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Palace Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was transferred to another post.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Palace Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was reassigned.

sentences.zh: 丁未，皇子生，少府劉勝之子也。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, a prince was born—it was the son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei a prince was born, said to be the son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng.

sentences.zh: [15]大赦天下。

translations.literal: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 贓汙淫盜，悉皆原除。

translations.literal: Corruption, licentiousness, and theft were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses of corruption, licentiousness, and theft were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 賜為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Those who became heirs for their fathers were granted one rank in nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had become heirs to their fathers were granted one noble rank.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以特進、左光祿大夫、護軍將軍建安王休仁為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Special Grand Master, Left Honored Grandee, and General of the Guard Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry with an office equal in ceremonial honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Special Grand Master, Left Honored Grandee, and General of the Guard Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was appointed Grand Marshal Who Pacifies the Cavalry with an office equal in ceremonial honor to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 戊午，南平王敬猷、廬陵王敬先、安南侯敬淵並賜死。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Prince of Nanping Jingyou, Prince of Luling Jingxian, and Marquis of Annan Jingyuan were all ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Prince of Nanping Jingyou, Prince of Luling Jingxian, and Marquis of Annan Jingyuan were all ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 時帝凶悖日甚，誅殺相繼，內外百司，不保首領。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor's ferocity and perversity grew daily; executions followed one upon another, and within and without the hundred offices none could keep his head.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor's cruelty and perversity grew worse by the day. Executions came one after another, and throughout the court no officeholder could be sure of keeping his head.

sentences.zh: 先是訛言云：「湘中出天子。

translations.literal: Earlier a false report had said: "A Son of Heaven will arise in Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a rumor had spread: "A Son of Heaven will arise in Xiang."

sentences.zh: 」帝將南巡荊、湘二州以厭之。

translations.literal: " The emperor intended to tour Jing and Xiang provinces in the south to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang provinces to counter the omen.

sentences.zh: 先欲誅諸叔，然後發引。

translations.literal: He first wished to execute all his uncles, and only then set out on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He meant first to kill all his uncles and only then depart on the tour.

sentences.zh: 太宗與左右阮佃夫、王道隆、李道兒密結帝左右壽寂之、姜產之等十一人，謀共廢帝。

translations.literal: Taizong secretly joined with his attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er to bind eleven men among the emperor's close attendants, including Shou Jizhi and Jiang Chanzhi, in a plot to depose the emperor together.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong secretly allied with his attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er to win over eleven of the emperor's close attendants, including Shou Jizhi and Jiang Chanzhi, in a joint plot to depose him.

sentences.zh: 戊午夜，帝於華林園竹林堂射鬼。

translations.literal: At midnight on the day wuwu, the emperor was at Bamboo Grove Hall in Hualin Garden shooting at ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on wuwu the emperor was in Bamboo Grove Hall at Hualin Garden, shooting at ghosts.

sentences.zh: 時巫覡云：「此堂有鬼。

translations.literal: At the time the shamans said: "This hall has ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans had said, "This hall is haunted."

sentences.zh: 」故帝自射之。

translations.literal: " Therefore the emperor shot at them himself.
translations.idiomatic: So the emperor went to shoot at them himself.

sentences.zh: 壽寂之懷刀直入，姜產之為副。

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi entered straight in with a knife concealed on his person; Jiang Chanzhi was his second.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi entered directly with a knife hidden on his person, with Jiang Chanzhi as his second.

sentences.zh: 帝欲走，寂之追而殞之。

translations.literal: The emperor tried to flee; Jizhi pursued him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried to run; Jizhi pursued him and struck him down.

sentences.zh: 時年十七。

translations.literal: He was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令曰：

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an order saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an edict, saying:

sentences.zh: 司徒領護軍八座：子業雖曰嫡長，少稟凶毒，不仁不孝，著自髫齔。

translations.literal: Minister of Works, General of the Guard, and the Eight Excellencies: though Ziye is called the legitimate eldest son, from youth he received a vicious nature; unkind and unfilial, this has been evident since he was a child.
translations.idiomatic: To the Minister of Works, General of the Guard, and the Eight Excellencies: though Ziye is called the legitimate eldest son, from childhood he has shown a vicious nature—unkind and unfilial, evident since he was a boy.

sentences.zh: 孝武棄世，屬當辰曆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu left the world, the succession fell to him in its season.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, the throne passed to him in due season.

sentences.zh: 自梓宮在殯，喜容靦然，天罰重離，歡恣滋甚。

translations.literal: From the time the imperial coffin lay in mourning, his face was calm and pleased; heaven's punishment doubled his separation, and his wanton joy grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the imperial coffin lay in state his face was calm and pleased; though heaven had doubled his bereavement, his wanton joy only grew.

sentences.zh: 逼以內外維持，忍虐未露，而凶慘難抑，一旦肆禍，遂縱戮上宰，殄害輔臣。

translations.literal: Forced by inner and outer constraints to hold back, his cruelty was not yet exposed; but his savage brutality could not be checked, and in a single day he unleashed disaster, wantonly slaughtering the chief ministers and destroying the assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by constraints within and without, he still hid his cruelty for a time; but his savage brutality could not be restrained, and in one day he unleashed catastrophe—murdering the chief ministers and destroying his chief advisers.

sentences.zh: 子鸞兄弟，先帝鍾愛，含怨既往，枉加屠酷。

translations.literal: Ziluan and his brothers were dearly loved by the late emperor; nursing old grievances, he wrongly subjected them to cruel slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Ziluan and his brothers had been dearly loved by the late emperor; nursing old resentments, the emperor wrongly put them to cruel death.

sentences.zh: 昶茂親作扞，橫相徵討。

translations.literal: Chang, a close kinsman, made a defense; yet he was attacked and punished without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, a close kinsman, had stood on his defense, yet was attacked and punished without cause.

sentences.zh: 新蔡公主逼離夫族，幽置深宮，詭云薨殞。

translations.literal: Princess of Xincai was torn from her husband's clan, shut away in the deep palace, and falsely reported to have died.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Xincai was torn from her husband's family, shut in the inner palace, and falsely announced to have died.

sentences.zh: 襄事甫爾，喪禮頓釋，昏酣長夜，庶事傾遺。

translations.literal: The mourning for the late emperor had barely ended when funeral rites were abruptly cast aside; drunken through the long night, the myriad affairs of state were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had mourning for the late emperor begun when funeral rites were cast aside; drunk through the long night, he let the affairs of state fall away.

sentences.zh: 朝賢舊勳，棄若遺土。

translations.literal: Court worthies and old merit-holders he cast off like discarded earth.
translations.idiomatic: Court worthies and old merit-holders he discarded like thrown-away soil.

sentences.zh: 管絃不輟，珍羞備膳。

translations.literal: Pipes and strings never ceased; delicacies filled every meal.
translations.idiomatic: Music never ceased; every meal was heaped with delicacies.

sentences.zh: 詈辱祖考，以為戲謔。

translations.literal: He cursed and insulted his ancestors, taking it as sport.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed and insulted his ancestors for amusement.

sentences.zh: 行游莫止，淫縱無度。

translations.literal: His travels knew no stop; his lewdness and excess had no limit.
translations.idiomatic: His wanderings knew no end; his lewdness and excess had no bounds.

sentences.zh: 肆宴園陵，規圖發掘。

translations.literal: He feasted freely in the imperial parks and tombs and plotted to excavate them.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted in the imperial parks and tombs and plotted to dig them up.

sentences.zh: 誅剪無辜，籍略婦女。

translations.literal: He executed and cut down the innocent and seized women by force.
translations.idiomatic: He killed the innocent and seized women by force.

sentences.zh: 建樹偽豎，莫知誰息。

translations.literal: He set up false attendants, and no one knew whose child they were.
translations.idiomatic: He installed false attendants whose parentage no one could tell.

sentences.zh: 拜嬪立后，慶過恒典。

translations.literal: In appointing consorts and establishing an empress, the celebrations exceeded the constant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing consorts and raising an empress, the celebrations exceeded all precedent.

sentences.zh: 宗室密戚，遇若婢僕，鞭捶陵曳，無復尊卑。

translations.literal: Toward kinsmen of the imperial clan he behaved as toward maidservants, beating and dragging them with no regard for rank.
translations.idiomatic: Toward imperial kinsmen he acted as toward maidservants, beating and dragging them without regard for rank.

sentences.zh: 南平一門，特鍾其酷。

translations.literal: The house of Nanping alone received his cruelty in special measure.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Nanping alone bore the full brunt of his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 反天滅理，顯暴萬端。

translations.literal: He turned against heaven and extinguished principle; his open violence had ten thousand forms.
translations.idiomatic: He turned against heaven and extinguished moral principle; his open violence took ten thousand forms.

sentences.zh: 苛罰酷令，終無紀極，夏桀、殷辛，未足以譬。

translations.literal: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no end or limit; Xia Jie and Yin Xin would not suffice for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no limit; not even Xia Jie and King Zhou of Shang would suffice for comparison.

sentences.zh: 闔朝業業，人不自保，百姓遑遑，手足靡厝。

translations.literal: The whole court was fearful; no man could preserve his life; the common people were in panic, with nowhere to set hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court trembled and no man could be sure of his life; the people were in panic, with nowhere to set hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 行穢禽獸，罪盈三千。

translations.literal: His conduct was filthy as a beast's; his offenses filled the three thousand categories.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was filthier than a beast's; his offenses filled every category of crime.

sentences.zh: 高祖之業將泯，七廟之享幾絕。

translations.literal: The enterprise of the High Ancestor was about to perish; the sacrifices of the seven temples were nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor's enterprise was nearly extinguished; the sacrifices of the seven temples were almost cut off.

sentences.zh: 吾老疾沈篤，每規禍鴆，憂煎漏刻，氣命無幾。

translations.literal: I am old and my illness deep; each day I foresee calamity and poison; worry burns through every moment, and my breath and life will not long remain.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and gravely ill; each day I foresee disaster; worry consumes every moment, and my life will not long endure.

sentences.zh: 開闢以降，所未嘗聞。

translations.literal: Since the opening of the age, such a thing has never been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Since the beginning of the age, nothing like this has ever been heard.

sentences.zh: 遠近思奮，十室而九。

translations.literal: Near and far yearn to rise up; nine houses in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far the people yearn to rise up—nine households in ten.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍湘東王體自太祖，天縱英聖，文皇鍾愛，寵冠列藩。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu derives his person from the Great Ancestor; heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity; Emperor Wen cherished him, and his favor surpassed all the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Prince of Xiangdong Yu descends from the Great Ancestor; heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity, and Emperor Wen cherished him above all other princes.

sentences.zh: 吾早識神睿，特兼常禮。

translations.literal: I early recognized his divine keenness and treated him with special courtesy beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: I recognized his keen intelligence early and treated him with courtesy beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 潛運宏規，義士投袂，獨夫既殞，懸首白旗，社稷再興，宗祏永固，人鬼屬心，大命允集。

translations.literal: He secretly carried out a great design; men of righteousness flung aside their sleeves; once the tyrant had fallen, his head hung from the white flag; the altars of state were renewed, the ancestral temple made secure forever; men and spirits turned their hearts to him, and the great mandate was justly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly carried out a great design; men of righteousness answered the call; once the tyrant had fallen, his head hung from the white flag; the altars were renewed and the ancestral temple secured; men and spirits turned to him, and the great mandate was justly his.

sentences.zh: 且勳德高邈，大業攸歸，宜遵漢、晉，纂承皇極。

translations.literal: Moreover his merit and virtue are high and far; the great enterprise returns to him; he should follow Han and Jin and succeed to the imperial apex.
translations.idiomatic: His merit and virtue are lofty; the great enterprise belongs to him; he should follow the precedents of Han and Jin and ascend the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 主者詳舊典以時奉行。

translations.literal: Those in charge should examine the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Let those in charge examine the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.

sentences.zh: 未亡人餘年不幸嬰此百艱，永尋情事，雖存若殞。

translations.literal: I, the not-yet-dead, in my remaining years have unhappily encountered this hundredfold calamity; forever recalling the circumstances, though I live it is as if I had perished.
translations.idiomatic: I, who am not yet dead, in my remaining years have met this hundredfold calamity; whenever I recall what has happened, though I still live I am as one already dead.

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What can be done!

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What can be done now!
translations.idiomatic: What is left to be done!

sentences.zh: 葬廢帝丹陽秣陵縣南郊壇西。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝幼而狷急，在東宮每為世祖所責。

translations.literal: The emperor from youth was narrow and quick-tempered; in the Eastern Palace he was often rebuked by Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood the emperor was narrow and quick-tempered; in the Eastern Palace Shizu often rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 世祖西巡，子業啟參承起居，書迹不謹，上詰讓之。

translations.literal: When Shizu toured the west, Ziye submitted reports on attending to his health and daily routine; his writing was careless, and the emperor questioned and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu toured the west, Ziye sent memorials on attending to his health and routine; his handwriting was careless, and the emperor questioned and reproached him.

sentences.zh: 子業啟事陳謝，上又答曰：「書不長進，此是一條耳。

translations.literal: Ziye submitted a memorial apologizing; the emperor again replied: "Your writing does not improve—this is one matter alone.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye submitted a memorial of apology; the emperor replied again: "Your writing never improves—that is one thing alone.

sentences.zh: 聞汝素都懈怠，狷戾日甚，何以頑固乃爾邪！

translations.literal: I hear you have always been idle and lax, and your perversity grows worse day by day—why are you so obstinately stubborn!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have always been idle and lax, and your perversity grows worse by the day—why must you be so stubbornly set in your ways!"

sentences.zh: 」初踐阼，受璽紱，悖然無哀容。

translations.literal: " When he first ascended the throne and received the seal and ribbon, he showed no grieving countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When he first ascended the throne and received the seal and ribbon, his face showed no grief.

sentences.zh: 始猶難諸大臣及戴法興等，既殺法興，諸大臣莫不震懾。

translations.literal: At first he still found the great ministers and Dai Faxing difficult to deal with; once Faxing had been killed, none of the great ministers was not shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: At first he still found the great ministers and Dai Faxing hard to manage; once Faxing was killed, every great minister trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 於是又誅羣公。

translations.literal: Then he also executed the host of nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Then he executed the whole company of nobles as well.

sentences.zh: 元凱以下，皆被毆捶牽曳。

translations.literal: From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten and dragged about.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan Kai on down, every one of them was beaten and dragged about.

sentences.zh: 內外危懼，殿省騷然。

translations.literal: Within and without there was peril; the palace offices were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court was in peril; the palace offices were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 初太后疾篤，遣呼帝。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager first fell gravely ill, she sent to summon the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager first fell gravely ill, she sent for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「病人間多鬼，可畏，那可往。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sickrooms have many ghosts—it is fearful; how could I go there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sickrooms are full of ghosts—it is frightening; how could I go there?"

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，語侍者：「將刀來，破我腹，那得生如此寧馨兒！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager grew angry and told her attendants: "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have borne such a precious little darling!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager flew into a rage and told her attendants, "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have given birth to such a precious darling!"

sentences.zh: 」及太后崩後數日，帝夢太后謂之曰：「汝不孝不仁，本無人君之相。

translations.literal: " Several days after the Empress Dowager died, the emperor dreamed that the Empress Dowager said to him: "You are unfilial and unkind; you never had the appearance of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after the Empress Dowager died, the emperor dreamed that she said to him, "You are unfilial and unkind; you never had the look of a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 子尚愚悖如此，亦非運祚所及。

translations.literal: Zishang is so foolish and perverse that he too is not within the span of fortune's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zishang is so foolish and perverse that even he lies outside the span of fortune's favor.

sentences.zh: 孝武險虐滅道，怨結人神，兒子雖多，並無天命。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was dangerous and cruel and extinguished the Way; resentment bound men and spirits; though he had many sons, none had heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was dangerous, cruel, and extinguished the Way; his deeds bound resentment among men and spirits; though he had many sons, none possessed heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 大運所歸，應還文帝之子。

translations.literal: The great fortune returns to the sons of Emperor Wen."
translations.idiomatic: The great fortune belongs to the sons of Emperor Wen."

sentences.zh: 」其後湘東王紹位，果文帝子也。

translations.literal: " Afterward Prince of Xiangdong Yu succeeded to the throne—and he was indeed a son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Prince of Xiangdong Yu succeeded to the throne—and he was indeed a son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 故帝聚諸叔京邑，慮在外為患。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing they would become a threat if left outside.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing trouble if they remained outside.

sentences.zh: 山陰公主淫恣過度，謂帝曰：「妾與陛下，雖男女有殊，俱託體先帝。

translations.literal: Princess of Shanyin was licentious beyond measure and said to the emperor: "Your subject and Your Majesty, though male and female differ, both owe our bodies to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Shanyin was licentious beyond all bounds and said to the emperor, "Your Majesty and I, though man and woman differ, both owe our bodies to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 陛下六宮萬數，而妾唯駙馬一人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ten thousand women in the six palaces, while I have only one husband by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ten thousand women in the six palaces, while I have only one husband.

sentences.zh: 事不均平，一何至此！

translations.literal: The affair is so unequal—how can it have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The disparity is so great—how can it have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃為主置面首左右三十人；

translations.literal: " The emperor then set up thirty male favorites at her left and right;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then provided her with thirty male favorites at her left and right;

sentences.zh: 進爵會稽郡長公主，秩同郡王，食湯沐邑二千戶，[16]給鼓吹一部，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: her rank was advanced to Princess of Kuaiji commandery with precedence equal to a prince of a commandery, with a bath-and-music fief of two thousand households, [16] one set of martial music granted, and twenty ceremonial swords added.
translations.idiomatic: she was advanced to Princess of Kuaiji commandery with rank equal to a commandery prince, granted a bath-and-music fief of two thousand households, [16] given one set of martial music, and twenty ceremonial swords besides.

sentences.zh: 帝每出，與朝臣常共陪輦。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, she commonly shared the imperial carriage with the court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went out, she commonly rode in the same carriage as the court ministers.

sentences.zh: 主以吏部郎褚淵貌美，就帝請以自侍，帝許之。

translations.literal: The princess, finding Lang of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan handsome, asked the emperor that he serve her; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The princess, finding Lang of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan handsome, asked the emperor to let him attend her; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 淵侍主十日，備見逼迫，誓死不回，遂得免。

translations.literal: Yuan attended the princess for ten days, was fully subjected to coercion, swore he would rather die than yield, and so was released.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan attended her for ten days, was pressed in every way, swore he would die rather than yield, and was at last released.

sentences.zh: 帝所幸閹人華願兒，官至散騎常侍，加將軍帶郡。

translations.literal: The eunuch Hua Yuan'er, whom the emperor favored, reached the post of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and was made a general with a commandery attached.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Hua Yuan'er, whom the emperor favored, rose to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and was made a general with a commandery attached.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書，[17]頗識古事，自造世祖誄及雜篇章，往往有辭采。

translations.literal: The emperor from youth loved reading [17] and knew many ancient matters; he himself composed Shizu's dirge and miscellaneous pieces, which often had literary color.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor loved reading [17] and knew many stories of antiquity; he himself composed Shizu's dirge and other pieces, which often showed literary polish.

sentences.zh: 以魏武帝有發丘中郎將、摸金校尉，乃置此二官。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had the offices of Director Who Opens Tombs and Colonel Who Seizes Gold, he established these two offices.
translations.idiomatic: Because Cao Cao had created the offices of Director Who Opens Tombs and Colonel Who Seizes Gold, he established these two posts.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were placed in charge of them.

sentences.zh: [18]其餘事迹，分見諸列傳。

translations.literal: [18] His remaining deeds are set forth separately in the various biographies.
translations.idiomatic: [18] His remaining deeds are set forth separately in the various biographies.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：廢帝之事行著于篇。

translations.literal: The historian says: The deeds of the Deposed Emperor are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: The deeds of the Deposed Emperor are set forth in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 若夫武王數殷紂之釁，不能絓其萬一；

translations.literal: As for King Wu numbering the offenses of King Zhou of Shang, he could not bind up one part in ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu counted the offenses of King Zhou of Shang, he could not capture one ten-thousandth of them;

sentences.zh: 霍光書昌邑之過，未足舉其毫釐。

translations.literal: when Huo Guang wrote the faults of Marquis of Haihun, he did not suffice to raise one hair's breadth of them.
translations.idiomatic: when Huo Guang recorded the faults of the Marquis of Haihun, he did not suffice to note one hair's breadth of them.

sentences.zh: 假以中才之君，有一于此，足以霣社殘宗，汚宮瀦廟，況總斯惡以萃一人之體乎！

translations.literal: Suppose a ruler of middling talent had one of these—it would be enough to overthrow the altars and ruin the clan, defile the palace and flood the temple; how much more when all these evils were gathered in a single person's body!
translations.idiomatic: Had a ruler of middling talent shown even one such trait, it would have been enough to overthrow the altars, ruin the clan, and defile palace and temple—how much more when every such evil was gathered in one man's person!

sentences.zh: 其得亡亦為幸矣。

translations.literal: That he escaped destruction was also a piece of good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That the dynasty escaped destruction at his hands was itself a kind of fortune.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 出居東宮 各本並脫「居」字，據元龜二五六補。

translations.literal: "Moved out to dwell in the Eastern Palace": All editions omit the character "dwell"; restored according to Yuan ce 256.
translations.idiomatic: "Moved out to the Eastern Palace": All editions drop the word "dwell"; restored from Yuan ce 256.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史 「南豫」子仁傳作「南兗」。

translations.literal: Director of Danyang Prince of Yongjia Ziren was made Inspector of Southern Yu: In Ziren's biography this reads "Southern Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Director of Danyang Prince of Yongjia Ziren as Inspector of Southern Yu: his biography has Southern Yan instead.

sentences.zh: 繁而傷治 「傷」各本並作「作」，據元龜一九一改。

translations.literal: "Elaborate and harmful to governance": In all editions "harmful" appears as "made"; emended according to Yuan ce 191.
translations.idiomatic: "Elaborate and harmful to governance": every edition reads "made" for "harmful"; corrected per Yuan ce 191.

sentences.zh: 氣緯舛互 「互」各本並作「玄」，蓋形近而譌，今改正。

translations.literal: "The qi-lines are at odds": In all editions "at odds" appears as "mysterious"; likely a graphic error near in form—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: "The qi-lines are at odds": all editions have "mysterious" for "at odds," probably a graphic confusion—corrected here.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍青冀二州刺史 各本「鎮北將軍」下並衍「南徐州刺史新安王子鸞為」十一字。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Wang Xuanmo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji: Below "General Who Pacifies the North" all editions interpolate the eleven characters "Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji: all editions wrongly insert "Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was" after "General Who Pacifies the North."

sentences.zh: 按新安王子鸞傳，不言曾為青、冀二州刺史，而王玄謨傳，言玄謨時徙為青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: According to the biography of Prince of Xin'an Ziluan, it does not say he ever served as Inspector of Qing and Ji, whereas Wang Xuanmo's biography says Xuanmo was at that time transferred to Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ziluan's biography never makes him Inspector of Qing and Ji, while Xuanmo's biography says he was transferred there at the time.

sentences.zh: 今訂正。

translations.literal: Now emended.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 己丑 各本並作「己未」。

translations.literal: Jichou: In all editions this reads "jiwei."
translations.idiomatic: Jichou: every edition reads jiwei instead.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，二十三日己丑，無己未、乙丑。

translations.literal: For this month dingmao was the new moon; the twenty-third day was jichou—there was no jiwei or yichou.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on dingmao; the twenty-third day was jichou—neither jiwei nor yichou occurred.

sentences.zh: 今據建康實錄及通鑑改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected according to the Jiankang shilu and Zizhi tongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected here according to the Jiankang shilu and Zizhi tongjian.

sentences.zh: 庚寅 各本並作「庚子」。

translations.literal: Gengyin: In all editions this reads "gengzi."
translations.idiomatic: Gengyin: all editions read gengzi.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，無庚子，二十三日己丑後，二十四日有庚寅。

translations.literal: For this month dingmao was the new moon—there was no gengzi; after the twenty-third day jichou, the twenty-fourth day was gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on dingmao, so there was no gengzi; jichou was the twenty-third day and gengyin the twenty-fourth.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected here.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史 「宗越」書中多誤作「宋越」，今據宗越傳改正。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Si: In the book "Zong Yue" is often wrongly written as "Song Yue"; now corrected according to Zong Yue's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yue as Inspector of Si: the book often miswrites his name as Song Yue—corrected from his biography.

sentences.zh: 以下類此者皆逕改，不具校。

translations.literal: Similar cases below are emended directly without full collation.
translations.idiomatic: Similar cases below are corrected without separate notes.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射 「尚書僕射」各本作「尚書左僕射」，南史無「左」字。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing: In all editions this reads "Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing"; the Nanshi has no "Left."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing: all editions add "Left," which the Nanshi omits.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘宋書札記云：「左字衍，當據南史刪。

translations.literal: Li Ciming's Song shu zhaji says: "The character Left is superfluous and should be deleted according to the Nanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming's Song shu zhaji notes: "Left is redundant and should be dropped per the Nanshi."

sentences.zh: 」按是時但置尚書僕射，不分立左右。

translations.literal: " At this time only a single Vice Director of the Masters of Writing was established, with no separate Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time there was only one Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, not separate Left and Right posts.

sentences.zh: 今據南史刪「左」字。

translations.literal: Now the character Left is deleted according to the Nanshi.
translations.idiomatic: The character Left is therefore deleted per the Nanshi.

sentences.zh: 減州郡縣田祿之半 宋本、三朝本、北監本、毛本及南史作「田祿」。

translations.literal: Reduce the field stipends of provinces, commanderies, and counties by half: The Song edition, Sanzhao edition, Beijian edition, Mao edition, and Nanshi read "field stipends."
translations.idiomatic: Halving field stipends in provinces, commanderies, and counties: the Song, Sanzhao, Beijian, and Mao editions and the Nanshi all read "field stipends."

sentences.zh: 殿本、局本作「田租」。

translations.literal: The Dian edition and Ju edition read "field rent."
translations.idiomatic: The Dian and Ju editions read "field rent."

sentences.zh: 建康實錄作「祿秩」。

translations.literal: The Jiankang shilu reads "stipend ranks."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiankang shilu has "stipend ranks."

sentences.zh: 按普減國內田租之半，非封建統治者所肯為，此必減州郡縣官吏田祿之半。

translations.literal: A general halving of land rent throughout the realm is not something a feudal ruler would undertake; this must mean halving the field stipends of officials in provinces, commanderies, and counties.
translations.idiomatic: A general halving of land rent empire-wide is not something a feudal ruler would do; the passage must mean halving officials' field stipends in provinces, commanderies, and counties.

sentences.zh: 故建康實錄改稱為「祿秩」。

translations.literal: Therefore the Jiankang shilu changed the wording to "stipend ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Jiankang shilu rephrases it as "stipend ranks."

sentences.zh: 衞將軍南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史 各本並脫「南」字。

translations.literal: General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was changed to Inspector of Yong: All editions omit the character "Southern."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangdong Yu, General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yu, reassigned as Inspector of Yong: all editions drop "Southern."

sentences.zh: 按明帝紀，永光元年為南豫州刺史，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: According to the annals of Emperor Ming, in the first year of Yongguang he was Inspector of Southern Yu, stationed at Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's annals show that in Yongguang year 1 he was Inspector of Southern Yu at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 又按州郡志，此時南豫州鎮姑孰，而豫州則未嘗以姑孰為州治。

translations.literal: According to the Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies, at this time Southern Yu was stationed at Gushu, whereas Yu province had never used Gushu as its seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies places Southern Yu at Gushu at this time, while Yu province had never had its seat there.

sentences.zh: 今據明帝紀補。

translations.literal: Now restored according to the annals of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: "Southern" is restored here from Emperor Ming's annals.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射顏師伯 「尚書左僕射」各本並作「尚書僕射」，據南史改，說見前。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo: In all editions this reads "Vice Director of the Masters of Writing"; emended according to the Nanshi, as explained above.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Yan Shibo: all editions lack "Left"; added back from the Nanshi, as noted above.

sentences.zh: 以鎮西大將軍豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍開府儀同三司 鎮西大將軍各本並作「鎮北大將軍」。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made General Who Pacifies the Army with an office equal in ceremonial honor to the Three Dukes: In all editions "General Who Pacifies the West" reads "General Who Pacifies the North."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army with Three-Dukes honors: all editions read General Who Pacifies the North instead of the West.

sentences.zh: 上九月辛亥下作鎮西大將軍，休祐傳亦作鎮西，今改正。

translations.literal: Above, under the ninth month on xinhai, it reads General Who Pacifies the West, and Xiuyou's biography also reads the West—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth-month xinhai entry and Xiuyou's biography both have General Who Pacifies the West—corrected here.

sentences.zh: 少府劉勝之子也 「劉勝」元龜一九七及二０七同本紀。

translations.literal: "The son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng": "Liu Sheng" appears thus in Yuan ce 197 and 207 in the same annals.
translations.idiomatic: "Son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng": Yuan ce 197 and 207 give Liu Sheng in the same annals.

sentences.zh: 符瑞志及始安王休仁傳、宋略、南史帝紀作劉矇，南史休仁傳作劉蒙。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Omens, the biography of Prince of Shian Xiuren, the Song lüe, and the Nanshi imperial annals read Liu Meng; the Nanshi biography of Xiuren reads Liu Meng in another form.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Omens, Xiuren's biography, the Song lüe, and the Nanshi annals have Liu Meng; the Nanshi biography of Xiuren gives another form of the name.

sentences.zh: 食湯沐邑二千戶 「食」各本並作「侯」。

translations.literal: "With a bath-and-music fief of two thousand households": In all editions "with" appears as "marquis."
translations.idiomatic: "Bath-and-music fief of two thousand households": all editions read "marquis" for "with."

sentences.zh: 據御覽一五二改。

translations.literal: Emended according to the Yulan 152.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected per the Yulan, juan 152.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書 「讀書」各本並作「講書」，據南史、元龜一九二、御覽一二八引改。

translations.literal: "The emperor from youth loved reading": In all editions "reading" appears as "lecturing"; emended according to the Nanshi, Yuan ce 192, and the Yulan 128 citation.
translations.idiomatic: "Loved reading from youth": all editions have "lecturing" instead of "reading"; corrected from the Nanshi, Yuan ce 192, and Yulan 128.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁山陽王休祐領之 各本並脫「休仁山陽王」五字，據南史補。

translations.literal: "Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge": All editions omit the five characters "Xiuren, Prince of Shanyang"; restored according to the Nanshi.
translations.idiomatic: "Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge": all editions omit "Xiuren, Prince of Shanyang"; restored from the Nanshi.

sentences.zh: 張燴讀史舉正云：「按建安王乃休仁，休祐則山陽王也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hui's Du shi juzheng says: "Prince of Jian'an is Xiuren, and Xiuyou is Prince of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui's Du shi juzheng explains: "Prince of Jian'an is Xiuren, and Xiuyou is Prince of Shanyang."

sentences.zh: 南史作『以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之』為是。」

translations.literal: The Nanshi's wording, "Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge," is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui concludes that the Nanshi reading, with both princes named, is the right one."
